boundary: Manual-backed routine and local-variable rules with a conservative counter-isolation policy. Tests prove offline prototype behavior; no new compiler or controller run, stack-layout authentication, or controller equivalence claim.

rules.implemented: Procedures can return without a value and scalar functions can return a checked value from a FOR body, including nested IF/WHILE/REPEAT/SELECT constructs and nested local FOR loops. The manual's index_value search example explicitly returns from a FOR loop.
rules.restriction: Every active counter must be a fresh VAR declared in the current routine. Global or formal-counter early-return behavior is blocked. Local frames are destroyed on routine exit; no claim about observable controller counter state, error paths or stack layout.

rules.implemented: Procedure and scalar-function calls are permitted when every active counter is a fresh routine-local variable. Other scalar, field and indexed references can be passed normally; local counter names shadow globals without sharing their storage. Callee frames use their own lexical declarations.
rules.restriction: Calls involving global or formal FOR counters are blocked. Existing call-effect and multi-argument evaluation-order checks remain active. Calls in FOR bounds remain blocked.

rules.implemented: Parenthesized counter arguments and expressions create independent scalar value temporaries. An INTEGER counter passed to a REAL formal is promoted by value under the existing exactness guard.
rules.restriction: Any active counter passed by reference is rejected with E_FOR_COUNTER, even to a currently read-only helper. This conservative policy keeps counter storage from escaping to a callee. Use parentheses for an INTEGER value argument.

rules.implemented: Inclusive bounds, initialization before final-bound evaluation, evaluate-once bounds and normal-completion counter clearing are unchanged. Runtime errors and step-budget failures unwind routine frames while retaining prior writes to reference/global storage.
rules.restriction: Direct counter writes, counter reuse in nested loops, labels/jumps inside FOR and ambiguous effectful indexed-result assignments remain blocked. Global-counter clearing on exceptional exits is not modeled or authenticated.

unresolved: Observable global/formal counter state when a routine returns or fails inside FOR
Permitting read-only counter references with a stronger per-parameter effect proof
User routine calls in FOR bound expressions and target/value evaluation order
Controller call stack, timing, alarms and release-specific behavior

abort_update.boundary: Bare ABORT terminates this offline instance without rollback; no task/action/condition or motion semantics. Routine effects propagate and frames unwind; direct FOR use requires fresh routine-local counters.

vector_routine_update.boundary: Exact initialized VECTOR results and writable value copies are supported. Bare protected orientation arguments, effect/order guards and controller boundaries remain; positional values use positional_routine_semantics.json.

structure_routine_update.boundary: Prior exact named STRUCTURE results and independent writable value copies are supported with full recursive initialization/type/capacity guards. Whole ARRAY values and controller behavior remain blocked; restricted results use array_routine_semantics.json; exact positional copies are covered in positional_routine_semantics.json.

positional_routine_update.boundary: Exact initialized CONFIG/XYZWPR/XYZWPREXT/POSITION and exact-width JOINTPOS results/writable value copies are supported. POSITION protection, CONFIG scalar value-only passing, effects and conversion-context guards remain; no frame, kinematic or controller behavior is supplied.

array_routine_update.boundary: Unsized 1D INTEGER/BOOLEAN/REAL/BYTE/SHORT results in direct assignment only, full initialized/known checked copies before cleanup and exact concrete destinations. BYTE/SHORT scalar arguments to INTEGER/REAL remain independent value copies. Broader ARRAY results and whole ARRAY value arguments remain blocked.
